Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

familiar adjective

familiar with, acquainted with (a subject or a place)

also familiar with, be familiar with, experienced in, know one’s way around, unfamiliar with

classical

Traupman 152
Cic. Off. 1.147: doctōs hominēs vel ūsū perītōs (Lewis & Short)

perītus, perīta, perītum

adjective, with the genitive (or the ablative)

experienced in, practised, skilled

Familiar with something from having done it; the opposite is imperītus.

Other words

  • gnārus, gnāra, gnārum — knowing, acquainted with

    adjective, with the genitive · also used · classical · Traupman 152; Plaut. Rud. 1.3.28: nec locī gnāra sum (Lewis & Short); Cic. Brut. 228: reī pūblicae

    Rare but classical (Lewis & Short); its opposite, ignārus, is the commoner word.

  • versātus in (+ abl.) — well versed in, at home in

    participle of versor, with in + ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Quinct. 3: in hāc multum et saepe versātus (Lewis & Short, s.v. versō); Cic. Rep. 3.4: virī in rērum pūblicārum varietāte versātī

    Familiar with a field from long dealing with it.

Examples

  • nec locī gnāra sum

    and I don’t know my way around herePlaut. Rud. 1.3.28 (Lewis & Short)

  • Ego hujus regiōnis imperītus sum; tū viam mōnstrā.

    I don’t know this area; you show the way.composed

See also familiar, know, skill, practical.

SourcesLewis & Short: peritus · Lewis & Short: gnarus · Lewis & Short: verso
